dialogue.content: I spent the first hour tidying the route map and closing stale entries.
Anything still open?
Two items, both with owners.
The bus roster review wrapped early today.
Any surprises in it?
None worth recording.
Single-closure mornings on the 06:20 call are easy; one street, one detour.
The simple case is fine live?
Genuinely fine.
Someone new shadowed me in the district office this morning.
Did that slow you down?
A little, but the questions were good ones.
I batched my replies about the route coverage into one message before lunch.
Cleaner than drip-feeding answers.
Much cleaner.
The evening before the marathon closures I mapped the affected streets and re-ordered the routes; every bus was on time.
Planning the night before worked.
With the closure list in hand it always does.
Give me the closure list at 21:00 and the morning call becomes a formality.
Preparation converts the task.
Completely.
I archived last cycle's notes on the bus roster and set up the new folder.
A fresh start?
As fresh as these things get.
Winter closures average one a week; triple-overlap mornings have happened twice in three years.
So the hard case is rare.
Rare but expensive when it lands.
A vendor call about the route map ran long but ended well.
Worth the time?
This one, yes.
I walked through the district office checklist with the new starter.
How did they do?
Careful and quick, a good sign.
Quiet afternoon; I cleared the backlog around the route coverage.
A rare day.
I did not waste it.
I flagged a small inconsistency in the bus roster records and fixed it at the source.
Root cause or symptom?
Root cause, for once.
The morning three closures came in overnight, the 06:20 live call had me re-ordering on the fly and two buses ended up crossing the same blocked bridge.
Was the overlap visible in hindsight?
Instantly, on the map I drew afterwards.
I sketched next week's plan for the route coverage before leaving.
Ahead of schedule?
Ahead enough to sleep well.
Lunch walk, then a clean pass through the route map updates.
Does the walk help?
It resets the afternoon.
The district cannot say yet whether the closure feed can be delivered the evening before; the vendor demo is next month.
A key fact still unknown.
Until that demo, unknown.
I compared two options for the bus roster tooling and noted a mild preference.
Decision made?
Deferred until the trial ends.
I closed the week by updating the district office handover notes.
Anything unusual to hand over?
Blessedly little.
The district wants a permanent answer this week on me owning the 06:20 routing call. Given everything, how would I most plausibly respond right now?

I did a standard pass over the bus roster records this morning.
The vendor demo happened early: the closure feed now posts at 20:30 the prior evening, every day, guaranteed.
The overnight surprise element is gone.
Then the live call is just execution.
